assign.request: Four mistakes reached the owner today (the site blanked twice by backticks inside a css() comment; the sidebar shipped visibly wrong with no whole-rail shot and no critic; the mastermind broke its own hook through a bash heredoc; fixed rem spacing at 3440 against the design tokens). Find why the skills and the process let each through and propose at most five changes ranked by mistakes prevented per line of text. Plus, from the owner mid-task: design the smallest 'decision auditor' — a system architect that audits judgment calls, triggered and graded by the mastermind, writing dated notes into each skill's log.
assign.now: reading the skills as an agent meets them, and the four task logs
steps: Read the brief and the minion skill
Read every SKILL.md, caveats and improvements as an agent meets them
Read the four task logs and the ledger, and measure what was actually loaded
Answer each case: what the agent had, why it was not enough
Rank at most five changes by mistakes prevented per line
Apply the fail-safe edits; write the rest as decisions
Design the auditor (the owner's fifth section) and write the skill

log.msg: MEASURED: none of the four sidebar tasks recorded loading css or layout. site-sidebar-tree and sidebar-repair recorded NO skill line at all; sidebar-filter recorded documentation/finish-task/check-claude-usage/fans/skill-improvement; tree-fixes recorded ui-test/documentation/finish-task. Their briefs told them to load css and layout.

MEASURED: the skill ledger under-records by construction. ledger.mjs attributes a SUBAGENT skill call only via a cache written by that agent PRIOR path-based edit resolution, so every reference skill loaded BEFORE the first edit is dropped. Evidence: 401 skill lines across 123 tasks since 2026-09-05, and ZERO new-task lines - the one skill that must run before the first edit.

MEASURED: all three sidebar landings certified in NUMBERS only - 0px drift across five page switches, 80/80 crawl checks, 12 rows narrowed to 2, 13 rows before and after, 0 console errors. Not one of them looked at the whole rail as a picture. A numeric proof cannot see a 46px row, an 80px label indent or a bordered card in a rail.

MEASURED: the sidebar-repair minion wrote the backtick rule into its own log at 14:54 (I BROKE THE LIVE SITE ... node --check after every .js write, before anything else) and broke the same file the same way at 15:05. A rule the agent had just written itself, in its own words, eleven minutes earlier, did not fire. That is the strongest evidence in the audit for a check over a sentence.

decision.about: PROPOSAL 1 - how a visible change proves it looks right, since three sidebar landings proved themselves entirely in numbers and every one of them was visibly wrong

options.say: finish-task section 2 replaces 'a picture when there is one' with: if anything visible changed, the outcome carries ONE picture of the WHOLE thing at 1920 - the whole rail, the whole page, the whole card wall, never a crop - plus one sentence saying what a stranger sees in it. A crop is extra, never the proof.
leave finish-task alone and have the mastermind demand the shot in each brief that touches something visible

decision.because: the three sidebar briefs already asked for proof and got 0px drift, 80/80 crawl checks, 12 rows narrowed to 2 and 0 console errors - all true, none of them able to see a 46px row or a bordered card in a rail. The builders kept one 170px crop between them. A brief-by-brief rule is forgotten exactly when the task looks small (tree-fixes was 'four small items'), and the one place every task passes through is the landing. Costs 2 lines in the skill and about 30 seconds a task; the mastermind then has a picture to open at harvest, which is the check that actually fires.
decision.alternative_cost: a required step is paid by every future task - the reason this is a proposal, not an edit

decision.about: PROPOSAL 2 - where a harness trap must live so the agent who needs it sees it: the mastermind broke its own ledger hook with a bash heredoc, a trap written down in the minion skill, which the mastermind does not load

options.say: two lines in CLAUDE.md's 'Traps that never throw' - the one file EVERY agent gets, mastermind included: (a) write files with the Write tool, never a bash heredoc (it eats one backslash layer and dies on an apostrophe; four times in two days); (b) a .js write that stops parsing blanks every page that imports it - the syntax guard will block you, believe it. Pay for them by cutting the 6-line heredoc paragraph in code#7 and tightening the minion bullet.
leave the traps in the code and minion skills and accept that an agent loading neither keeps hitting them

decision.because: a trap belongs in the channel with 100 percent readership, and CLAUDE.md is the only one - skills are opt-in and the mastermind opts into none of the craft skills. Net text goes DOWN if the two duplicated copies are cut in the same pass. CLAUDE.md says do not edit without asking, so this is the owner's line to approve, and I have written the exact wording rather than a description of it.

decision.about: PROPOSAL 3 - two of today's four mistakes (the broken hook, the fixed-rem spacing at 3440) were the mastermind's own hands-on edits, made without loading code, css or layout

options.say: one line in the mastermind skill: the mastermind's own writes are briefs, reports, board cards and task logs. A hook, a stylesheet, a page, a jsonl script goes to a minion that loads the craft skills - even a two-line fix, even when it is faster to do it. The owner's own rule from 2026-09-04 (the mastermind relays, never executes) exists in memory and is not in the skill.
the mastermind may edit code, but must load code/css/layout first

decision.because: one line prevents two of today's four mistakes, the best ratio in this audit. The load-first version costs the mastermind thousands of tokens of reference text per small fix and still leaves it working at the wrong altitude while minions wait for briefs. The exception worth writing is emergencies - a live page is blank and a minion would take minutes - and even then the fix is the smallest possible revert, then a minion.
decision.alternative_cost: there will be moments when a one-word fix waits on a spawn; the audit says that is cheaper than the two mistakes it prevents

decision.about: PROPOSAL 4 - the system cannot currently tell 'the rule was loaded and ignored' from 'the skill was never loaded', which is the whole question this audit had to answer

options.say: the landing assign carries skills: [names the agent loaded]; the mastermind compares it at harvest with what the brief asked for, in one glance
change ledger.mjs so a subagent's Skill call resolves its task before its first edit

decision.because: MEASURED: 401 skill lines across 123 tasks since 2026-09-05 and ZERO new-task lines, because ledger.mjs attributes a subagent's Skill call only through a cache written by that agent's first path-based EDIT - so every reference skill loaded up front (code, layout, css, and new-task itself) is invisible. Two of the four sidebar tasks show no skill line at all. Fixing the hook means guessing a subagent's task before it has touched a file, and a wrong guess writes into a sibling's live log - the exact failure the cache was built to stop (2026-08-18, four cases). One self-reported field is honest, costs one line, and is checkable against the brief.

decision.about: PROPOSAL 5 / the owner's decision auditor - the smallest shape that produces correct outcomes

options.say: a new .claude/skills/auditor/ (81 lines, written today, loaded by nobody else) + the misuse report is ONE dated signed line in that skill's existing improvements.md + the mastermind triggers per mistake and grades the audit in one line afterwards + resume the same auditor by SendMessage while it lives, fresh spawn when it does not
a new notes.md beside every skill's improvements.md, for opinions as distinct from proposed changes
no auditor skill at all - the mastermind section written today already carries the procedure

decision.because: the evidence for a skill is already recorded three ways (the ledger's skill lines, each improvements.md, and the decision lines in every task log) - a per-skill notes file would split that evidence in two and create fifteen near-empty files nobody reads, so the note goes in improvements.md with a widened one-line format that allows a plain opinion, signed and dated. A skill rather than a section because the auditor is a ROLE with its own reading list (CLAUDE.md plus every SKILL.md) and its own stop rule, and a new skill dir changes nothing for any other agent; the mastermind's own section should shrink to two lines pointing here once this is approved. Persistence is worth it within a day - a woken auditor skips about 2,300 lines of re-reading - but never worth blocking on: a resumed transcript can vanish after about 45 idle minutes, so the rule is wake it, and spawn fresh if it does not answer.
decision.alternative_cost: an auditor that produces nothing is pure overhead - hence the grading line and the three-strikes rule in the skill

log.msg: Trade-off on my own page, written down rather than hidden: the four case cards are a .grid.auto wall with --column 18rem, which is 4-up at 1920 and 3440 and 3+1 at about 1600. The layout skill says a wall with a KNOWN count should write its column counts out - that needs a stylesheet and a new class for one report page, so I took the orphan row at mid widths instead. Also worth knowing for proposal 1: a Playwright fullPage shot of this site captures ONE viewport, because .app is a height-constrained shell that scrolls inside - the whole-thing shot needs a tall viewport (I used 1600x2800), not fullPage.

assign.now: landing - the page renders clean at 1920 and 400, no console errors, and I looked at the whole thing in one tall shot

assign.outcome:
**Four mistakes, one pattern: in three of the four the rule existed, was clearly written, and the agent never loaded the skill it lives in.** Adding words to those skills would have changed nothing.

- **Case 1, the site blanked twice.** The minion wrote the backtick rule into its own log at 14:54, in its own words, and broke the same file the same way at 15:05. A rule in four places did not fire; `.claude/hooks/syntax-guard.mjs` does. 
- **Case 2, the sidebar shipped wrong.** All three landings certified in numbers — 0px drift, 80/80 crawl checks, 12 rows narrowed to 2, 0 console errors, all true — and none of those can see a 46px row. Not one of the four sidebar tasks recorded loading `css` or `layout`.
- **Cases 3 and 4, the broken hook and the fixed-rem spacing.** Both were the mastermind editing by hand, having loaded none of the craft skills. One line fixes both.

**The page:** [/framework/ai/2026-09-19/mistake-audit/](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/mistake-audit/) — the four cases, the five ranked changes, and the owner's decision auditor. Shot of the whole thing: /framework/ai/2026-09-19/mistake-audit/shots/page-tall.png

**Applied (fail-safe):** `css/caveats.md`'s backtick line rewritten to name the comment, the symptom and the hook; the two `improvements.md` entries asking for it deleted (they are applied); one clause each in `code/SKILL.md` and `minion/SKILL.md`; new `.claude/skills/auditor/` (81 lines, loaded by nobody else). Net on the skills agents load: **−2 lines, ~360 words of duplicated backtick prose gone.**

**Waiting on the owner** (five `decision` lines, each with its alternative): 1 a visible change lands with one picture of the WHOLE thing · 2 the two harness traps move into CLAUDE.md, paid for by cutting the duplicates · 3 the mastermind writes no code (prevents cases 3 and 4 with one line) · 4 the landing names the skills actually loaded · 5 the auditor shape.

**Measured:** 401 skill lines across 123 tasks since 2026-09-05 and **zero** for `new-task` — `ledger.mjs` records a subagent's skill call only after its first edit, so every reference skill loaded up front is invisible. That is why "was the skill used correctly?" cannot be answered today, and it is proposal 4.

**Left deliberately:** the `css` and `layout` skills untouched (both already carry the rules these mistakes broke, with measurements — neither failing agent loaded them); the mastermind's own "audit a mistake" section untouched, it is theirs to shrink to a pointer; the case-card wall orphans one row at ~1600 (fixing it properly costs a stylesheet and a new class for one report page).
